title: Dataset format and packaging
summary: Turn libphonenumber XML and geocoding files into a compact on-device format
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Sources inspected and understood: PhoneNumberMetadata.xml (~979 KB, 245 territories, possibleLengths + nationalNumberPattern per country per type) and resources/geocoding (151 countries, 34 languages, 11 MB total, 6.6 MB for English alone).

Build the tooling that converts upstream libphonenumber data into a compact format the core reads directly.

WHY NOT PARSE XML AT RUNTIME: the iOS Call Directory and SMS filter extensions run under tight memory limits. Parsing a megabyte of XML to answer one question is not viable there.

REQUIREMENTS OF THE FORMAT:
- Fast lookup by country and number type; fast longest-prefix match for the geocoder.
- Memory-mappable or lazily loadable, so an extension can answer one question without loading everything.
- Self-describing and versioned, so the engine can run against a dataset it was not compiled against.
- Selective packaging: ship only the countries and languages needed, not all 11 MB. We control this.

DO NOT ASSUME A FIXED SHAPE (Guidelines §1): not every country defines every number type — uan appears in 63 territories, voicemail in 15, of 245. The converter and the reader must both handle types being absent, and must not hardcode the type list.

ALSO CARRIES: R7's UI language files ride the same packaging, so adding a language is not a release.

BUILD IT GENERAL: the format should describe "a versioned dataset", not "phone metadata". R1's daily spam list uses the same format later.

VALIDATION: the converter must verify what it produces — every territory present, patterns compile, prefix tries resolve — because a silently truncated dataset would make rules stop matching with no error.

tasks.title: Vendor the libphonenumber source data into the repo
tasks.description:
UNBLOCKS P004(F002), the prefix-to-place geocoder, which cannot start without this data.

WHAT WAS FOUND, 2026-09-10. F002 says "the phonenumber crate has no geocoder". True of its API, but MISLEADING about the data: the crate ships assets/geocoding — 34 languages, 151 country files under English — and assets/PhoneNumberMetadata.xml. Its build.rs compiles in ONLY the metadata XML. The geocoding files sit in the crate directory unused and unreachable from our code, and will not be in our app.

MEASURED:
- English geocoding: 269,380 prefix entries across 151 countries, 38,116 distinct place names, 6.6 MB of text.
- All 34 languages together: 11 MB.
- Coverage is wildly uneven. English 151 countries; Chinese 130,209 entries; Portuguese 12,237; German 6,545. ITALIAN COVERS EXACTLY TWO COUNTRIES (39 and 41). So R7's fallback to English is not an edge case, it is the normal path for most users.
- Format is trivial: `<full E.164 prefix>|<place name>` per line, sorted, with an Apache 2.0 header. Example from en/39.txt: `390122|Turin`.

GOAL. Bring the upstream data into the repository so builds are reproducible and do not reach into ~/.cargo.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. A vendored copy under a clear path (suggest data/upstream/), carrying both the geocoding tree and PhoneNumberMetadata.xml.
2. Provenance recorded next to it: which libphonenumber release, which crate version it came from, the date, and how to refresh it. Without this nobody can tell later whether the data matches the metadata the engine validates against — and if the two drift, place names describe prefixes that no longer exist.
3. Attribution. The data is Apache 2.0 from The Libphonenumber Authors. Keep the licence headers, and add a NOTICE or equivalent recording the source. This is redistribution, so it is not optional.
4. A check that the vendored data and the metadata the core actually uses came from the same libphonenumber version, failing loudly if not. The crate is phonenumber 0.3.10+9.0.33, where 9.0.33 is the upstream version — so the check has something concrete to compare against.

DECISION TO RECORD: take the data from the crate's own assets rather than fetching libphonenumber upstream. Upstream is newer, but the core validates numbers against the metadata compiled into the crate. If place data is newer than the number metadata, the geocoder will name prefixes the expander rejects. They must move together.

CONSTRAINTS.
- Guidelines §1: no country in code. This is data, and vendoring it is the point.
- Vendoring 11 MB is a deliberate repository cost. Take all languages, so choosing which to ship is a packaging decision (T-next) rather than a re-fetch.

DONE WHEN. The data is in the repo with provenance and attribution, the version check exists and passes, nothing reads from ~/.cargo, and a fresh clone can build and convert without network access.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED. Commit dfe329b.

data/upstream/ (new): the geocoding tree (34 languages, 151 English country files) and PhoneNumberMetadata.xml, copied verbatim. data/upstream/PROVENANCE.md, NOTICE, tools/check-vendored-data.sh, and a CI step running it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG IN THE PLAN. F002 says "the phonenumber crate has no geocoder (the phonenumber crate has none)". True of its API and misleading about its data: the crate ships assets/geocoding in full. Its build.rs compiles in only PhoneNumberMetadata.xml, so the place files sit in the crate directory unreachable from our code and would never reach the app. The gap was never "the data does not exist", it was "the data is not wired up" — a different and much smaller problem than the plan implies.

DECISION — copied from the crate, not fetched from libphonenumber upstream. Upstream runs ahead of the crate. The core validates numbers against the metadata compiled into the crate, so if place data were newer the geocoder would name prefixes the expander rejects, and a rule written against a city would stop matching with nothing logged and nothing on screen. Both halves must move together. tools/check-vendored-data.sh enforces it by comparing PROVENANCE.md against the phonenumber version in Cargo.lock.

DECISION — copied into the repo rather than read from ~/.cargo at build time, so a build does not depend on a developer's machine. Verified nothing outside the documented refresh command references that path.

DECISION — all 34 languages vendored, costing 12 MB of repository. Deliberate, so choosing which to ship is a packaging decision in T015 rather than a re-fetch.

COVERAGE, and it shapes the product rather than being a detail. English is the only near-complete language: 151 countries, 269,380 prefix entries, 38,116 distinct place names. Chinese has 130,209 entries but 2 countries. German 5 countries. ITALIAN COVERS EXACTLY TWO — Italy and Switzerland. So R7's fallback (user's language, then English, then bare prefix) is the normal path for most users, not an edge case, and the UI has to read that way. Recorded in PROVENANCE.md.

VERIFIED, including the failure modes — a check that only ever passes is worthless:
- Healthy tree passes and reports "libphonenumber 9.0.33, 34 languages, 151 English countries".
- A version mismatch between PROVENANCE.md and Cargo.lock is caught, naming both versions.
- A truncated English tree is caught, because everything falls back to English so an incomplete English tree breaks place names everywhere.
- A missing NOTICE is caught. This is Apache 2.0 data being redistributed, so attribution is a licence obligation, not tidiness.
- FRESH CLONE TESTED, not assumed: cloned to a temp directory, confirmed 151 English files present, `cargo build --offline` succeeded, and both lints pass in the clone.
- cargo test 98 pass, cargo fmt --check clean, §1 lint clean.

NOT DONE HERE. No converter and no compact format — that is P006(F003)/T015. Nothing in the core reads this data yet. The 38,116-vs-269,380 ratio is recorded because it is what the packed format should exploit, but nothing exploits it so far.

UNVERIFIED. The check compares version strings; it does not hash the data, so a hand-edited file under data/upstream would pass. Byte-level integrity is worth adding when the converter lands and has something to compare against.

tasks.title: Convert geocoding data into a compact versioned dataset
tasks.description:
DEPENDS ON P006(F003)/T014 for the vendored source.

GOAL. A build tool that turns the vendored text into a compact binary dataset the core reads directly, plus the validation that stops a broken one shipping.

WHY NOT SHIP THE TEXT. 6.6 MB for English alone, 269,380 lines to scan for one lookup. The measured shape says what the format should be: 269,380 prefix entries but only 38,116 distinct place names, so names belong in a deduplicated string table and entries become (prefix, name index). Sorted prefixes give longest-match by binary search — at most fifteen probes, since that is the longest an E.164 number gets.

WHERE THIS RUNS, and it is not where the phase assumed. The phase says the format must survive an iOS extension's memory limit. The geocoder does not run there: the Call Directory extension receives a finished list of numbers, and place names are an app-side concern — turning a place into a prefix when a rule is written, and showing a place for a number in the UI. Design for a phone app, not for the extension. Say so in the code, because the phase description currently implies otherwise.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. A converter, as a tool alongside the existing ones in tools/ or a cargo bin. Input: the vendored tree. Output: one dataset file per language.
2. A container that is SELF-DESCRIBING AND VERSIONED, and describes "a versioned dataset" rather than "geocoding" — R1's spam list and R7's UI strings ride the same format later, and R5 requires the engine to run against a dataset it was not compiled against. A magic number, a format version, the upstream data version, the language, and a table of contents.
3. Selective packaging: choose which languages and countries go into a build. English is the only near-complete one, so a sensible default is English plus whatever the user's language covers. Do not bake the choice into code.
4. VALIDATION THAT FAILS THE BUILD. Every country in the source appears in the output; counts match; prefixes are sorted, unique and parse as digits; every name index resolves. A silently truncated dataset makes rules stop matching with no error anywhere, which the phase calls out as close to undebuggable. CI has a note reserved for exactly this step.

CONSTRAINTS.
- Guidelines §1: no country, prefix or place name in code. Enumerate from the data.
- Do not assume a fixed shape: coverage per language is wildly uneven (English 151 countries, Italian 2), so absent countries are normal, not an error.
- Reproducible: the same input must produce a byte-identical output, or the version check in T014 means nothing.

EDGE CASES to test: a language covering two countries; a country whose file is only a licence header; duplicate prefixes within a file; a place name containing the delimiter; non-ASCII names, which most of the non-English data is; the longest prefix in the data; an empty language directory.

DONE WHEN. The converter produces a dataset for every vendored language, validation catches a deliberately truncated input, output is byte-reproducible, and cargo test / fmt / clippy -D warnings / the §1 lint pass.

checklist.title: Converter tool reading the vendored tree
Deduplicated string table plus sorted (prefix, name index) entries
Self-describing versioned container, general across dataset kinds
Selective packaging by language and country, not baked into code
Validation that fails the build on a truncated or inconsistent dataset
Documented that the geocoder is app-side, not extension-side
Edge cases: sparse language, header-only file, duplicate prefix, delimiter in name, non-ASCII, longest prefix, empty directory
cargo test, fmt, clippy -D warnings, no-hardcoded-numbering lint
